question: What was the main problem with most ancient birth control methods?

options.A: They were too expensive for ordinary citizens to purchase
options.B: They were frequently toxic, unreliable, or completely ineffective
options.C: They required advanced surgical equipment available only to royalty
options.D: They relied on electronic monitoring of the menstrual cycle

explanation: Ancient remedies relied a lot on guesswork and folk traditions, which often meant they didn't work well and could even be unsafe. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h2)

question: As a nurse, what common myth about weakness in cancer patients should you avoid?

options.A: Thinking it has no relationship to chemotherapy
options.B: Assuming it is simply due to aging or lack of effort
options.C: Believing it can only be cured by heavy weightlifting
options.D: Stating that it always resolves immediately after surgery

explanation: Never assume a weak patient is just being lazy or getting old! Cancer weakness comes from the disease, poor nutrition, and heavy treatments. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h4)

question: What happens during drug distribution in the body?

options.A: The liver breaks down the medicine into waste products
options.B: The gut absorbs a swallowed pill
options.C: The drug moves from the blood into various body tissues
options.D: The kidneys eliminate active drug molecules

explanation: Think of distribution as the drug's journey out of the bloodstream and into the body tissues where it's actually needed to work! You've got this. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T2#GNS125_U5_T2_h1)

question: What does a glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) test actually tell us about a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Average blood glucose control over the past two to three months
options.B: The exact blood sugar level at the exact moment of the blood draw
options.C: The total amount of insulin stored in the pancreatic beta cells
options.D: How quickly the kidneys are filtering sugar out into the urine

explanation: Think of the HbA1c test as a memory log! Because sugar sticks to red blood cells for their 120-day lifespan, this test shows us the big picture of how blood sugar has been managed over the last few months. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h7)

question: Which drug is given as the specific antidote for a severe paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Acetylcysteine
options.B: Naloxone
options.C: Flumazenil
options.D: Atropine

explanation: Acetylcysteine works like a rescue hero! It acts as a glutathione precursor, soaking up and detoxifying the harmful paracetamol breakdown product before it can ruin the liver. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h7)

question: Why are beta-blockers commonly prescribed for structural heart conditions?

options.A: To dilate peripheral arteries and eliminate all body fat
options.B: To slow the heart rate and allow better ventricular filling time
options.C: To stimulate faster electrical firing from the sinus node
options.D: To thin the blood and stop all clot formation instantly

explanation: Slowing the heart down gives the ventricles more time to relax and fill up with blood, while also giving the tired heart muscle a bit of a break. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h8)

question: Why are daily weight checks such an important nursing tool when managing fluid and electrolyte imbalances?

options.A: Body weight dictates the exact dosage of every routine antibiotic
options.B: Changes in weight provide a reliable daily measure of fluid gain or loss
options.C: Sudden weight loss always proves that kidney function has fully recovered
options.D: Weight records replace the need to monitor urinary output in bedridden patients

explanation: Spot on! A sudden change in weight over 24 hours isn't fat or muscle—it's almost always a shift in body water. Daily weights help us catch fluid overload early! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is a major direct cause of maternal mortality in Nigeria?

options.A: Severe bleeding after childbirth
options.B: Untreated childhood measles
options.C: Chronic adult asthma
options.D: Seasonal malaria outbreaks in men

explanation: Severe bleeding after delivery (known as postpartum hemorrhage) is one of the leading direct causes of maternal death. As a future nurse, knowing this helps you spot why rapid postpartum care is so vital. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h2)

question: When should you perform abdominal thrusts on a choking victim?

options.A: When the victim complains of a sore throat
options.B: When the victim cannot speak, cough, or breathe
options.C: When the victim feels a mild tickle in the throat
options.D: When the victim is coughing forcefully and loudly

explanation: If they can cough loudly, encourage them to keep coughing! Reserve abdominal thrusts for severe blockages where they cannot speak, cough, or breathe. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h6)

question: How do Hepatitis B and C viruses primarily cause damage inside the human body?

options.A: By blocking oxygen transport in red blood cells
options.B: By releasing toxins that paralyze skeletal muscles
options.C: By destroying CD4+ immune cells in the bloodstream
options.D: By targeting hepatocytes and triggering liver inflammation

explanation: Both Hepatitis B and C love to attack liver cells (hepatocytes), causing inflammation and gradual damage over time. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the typical duration of the postpartum period known as the puerperium?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: One year

explanation: The puerperium generally lasts for about six weeks after childbirth, which is the time required for maternal organs to return close to their pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h1)

question: What is the medical name for the condition where a baby's foot is twisted inward and downward?

options.A: Congenital talipes equinovarus
options.B: Developmental dysplasia of the hip
options.C: Spina bifida occulta
options.D: Osteogenesis imperfecta

explanation: That's just the fancy clinical term for clubfoot! You'll hear 'talipes equinovarus' a lot in your pediatric postings. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h4)

question: A patient died with an IV line in place and a coroner's post-mortem is requested. What should the nurse do with the line?

options.A: Hide the lines under the bedsheets
options.B: Remove all lines immediately to clean the skin
options.C: Leave all lines and tubes in place
options.D: Cut the tubing short and tape it down

explanation: For coroner's cases or potential legal investigations, invasive lines and tubes must be left intact for the pathologist. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: Why is nurse-led education for patients and visitors important for waste management?

options.A: To train family members how to incinerate trash in the hospital yard
options.B: To encourage visitors to bring their own waste bags from home
options.C: To prevent visitors from accidentally touching hazardous waste or opening bins
options.D: To reduce the hospital budget spent on buying cleaning detergents

explanation: Visitors often do not know clinical waste risks, so nursing guidance keeps them from touching contaminated materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: Why is it tricky that many STIs in women show no symptoms at all?

options.A: The immune system permanently attacks healthy tissues instead of the pathogen
options.B: Infected women unknowingly spread the infection and delay necessary treatment
options.C: Routine diagnostic tests consistently fail to detect silent infections
options.D: Asymptomatic infections immediately progress to systemic organ failure

explanation: When an infection causes no signs or pain, a woman has no reason to visit the clinic, letting the disease grow quietly and pass to others. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary condition treated using emergency inhaled bronchodilators?

options.A: Acute bronchospasm
options.B: Lower extremity deep vein thrombosis
options.C: Chronic bacterial skin infection
options.D: Severe iron-deficiency anemia

explanation: Bronchodilators relax tightened airway muscles, making them the primary treatment for sudden breathing constriction or asthma attacks. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h4)

question: A patient is deeply sad over losing a pet, but friends tell them to just get another one. What kind of grief is this?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Disenfranchised grief
options.C: Uncomplicated grief
options.D: Collective grief

explanation: Exactly! When people brush off a loss because they don't understand its value—like a pet—the person experiences disenfranchised grief because others don't validate their pain. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T5#GNS221_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why can a brain abscess cause symptoms that look just like a brain tumor?

options.A: It acts as a mass that takes up space and increases pressure inside the skull.
options.B: It causes the hair on the scalp to fall out rapidly.
options.C: It replaces normal brain cells with cancer cells.
options.D: It changes the genetic makeup of surrounding neurons over time.

explanation: A pocket of pus inside the head takes up physical space, just like a tumor. This raises the pressure inside the skull (ICP) and presses on nearby brain areas. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T17#GNS222_U3_T17_h3)

question: Which test is most helpful for checking acid-base balance after an asphyxial event?

options.A: Arterial blood gas analysis
options.B: Routine urinalysis dipstick
options.C: Serum electrolyte panel
options.D: Complete blood cell count

explanation: An ABG test is your best friend here. It gives you a direct look at the patient's blood pH, oxygen levels, and how well they are clearing out carbon dioxide. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T1#GNS112_U7_T1_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of Charting by Exception (CBE)?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any nursing signatures
options.B: It reduces redundant writing by focusing on abnormal findings
options.C: It prevents patients from reading their own medical charts
options.D: It allows nurses to skip physical head-to-toe assessments

explanation: That is right! CBE assumes everything is normal unless you write down an exception, which saves precious time on a busy shift. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is an effective communication technique when talking to a client with a neurologic speech delay?

options.A: Giving the client extra time to process and answer questions
options.B: Finishing every sentence quickly so the client does not get tired
options.C: Avoiding eye contact to reduce the client's social anxiety
options.D: Speaking in medical jargon to sound professional

explanation: Neurologic conditions often slow down processing speed, so patience and waiting for a response are essential for clear communication. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the typical duration of antibiotic therapy for osteomyelitis?

options.A: 3 to 5 days
options.B: 24 to 48 hours
options.C: 4 to 6 weeks or longer
options.D: Exactly one year

explanation: Because antibiotics penetrate bone tissue slowly, treatment requires a prolonged course, usually lasting several weeks to clear the infection fully. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h7)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support just as crucial as physical care for these clients?

options.A: Coping with a progressive, incurable disease often leads to depression and anxiety.
options.B: Clients with degenerative disorders never experience physical pain.
options.C: Emotional stress can directly reverse the genetic mutation in the DNA.
options.D: Psychological counseling replaces the need for any nutritional support.

explanation: Watching one's body slowly fail creates a heavy mental burden, making compassionate psychological support essential. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h7)

question: What kind of food is best to suggest for a patient suffering from painful mouth ulcers?

options.A: Hot, spicy, and crunchy snacks
options.B: Dry, salty crackers and toast
options.C: Acidic citrus fruits and juices
options.D: Cool, bland, and soft foods

explanation: Cool, soft, and gentle foods help keep the patient comfortable and avoid irritating sensitive sores. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h7)

question: How is a 'confirmed' case different from a 'suspected' case?

options.A: A confirmed case requires no medical isolation, unlike a suspected case
options.B: A suspected case means the patient has fully recovered from the illness
options.C: A suspected case is always more severe and infectious than a confirmed case
options.D: A confirmed case has laboratory proof of the pathogen, while a suspected case only has symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Lab results turn a 'suspected' case (based only on signs and symptoms) into a 'confirmed' case. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT helpful to include when charting about a patient's cough?

options.A: Factors that make the coughing worse
options.B: The color and amount of any sputum produced
options.C: The brand of soap used in the hospital room
options.D: Whether the cough is dry or productive

explanation: You got it! The soap brand won't change lung assessment findings, but details about sputum, triggers, and cough type are clinical gold! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h8)

question: What core toxicological principle states that virtually any substance can act as a poison if the quantity is large enough?

options.A: All chemicals are inherently lethal
options.B: The route determines toxicity
options.C: Metabolism prevents all toxicity
options.D: The dose makes the poison

explanation: Toxicology teaches that safety and toxicity depend on the amount of exposure, meaning harmless substances can become dangerous in excessive quantities. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h1)

question: Why is it crucial for nurses to monitor a patient's urine output in the hours following an IVP?

options.A: To calculate the exact amount of IV antibiotic therapy the client requires
options.B: To ensure the bladder has not ruptured from the pressure of the procedure
options.C: To prove that the patient is complying with strict fasting orders
options.D: To confirm that the kidneys are clearing the dye and not showing signs of failure

explanation: Good urine output tells us the kidneys are handling the dye well and keeps us ahead of any potential kidney stress. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T16#GNS221_U2_T16_h6)

question: What is a major duty of a medical social worker in a rehab setting?

options.A: Doing physical strength exercises with recovering patients
options.B: Conducting formal swallow studies for dysphagia patients
options.C: Prescribing pain medications and muscle relaxants
options.D: Checking home safety and connecting families to helpful resources

explanation: Social workers are fantastic advocates! They look at home environments and link families with community support, equipment, and funding. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h6)

question: A patient is having a panic attack and breathing way too fast. What are they at risk for?

options.A: Metabolic acidosis
options.B: Metabolic alkalosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Respiratory acidosis

explanation: Spot on! Breathing too fast blows off too much carbon dioxide. Losing too much acid makes the blood basic (alkaline), causing respiratory alkalosis. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h6)

question: Besides physical treatment, what else is an essential part of holistic post-abortion care?

options.A: Mandatory reporting of the client to local religious leaders
options.B: Empathetic emotional support and contraceptive counseling
options.C: Permanent hospital admission for psychological observation
options.D: Informing the client's family members about the medical history

explanation: Good nursing looks at the whole person! Along with healing the body, we offer kind emotional support and teach them about family planning for the future. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h8)

question: Why are abstinence-only education programs often insufficient for protecting teenagers?

options.A: They force schools to close down health clinics
options.B: They cause physical delays in the maturation of the prefrontal cortex
options.C: They encourage teenagers to read explicit material online instead
options.D: They fail to give youth who become active the practical skills needed to prevent diseases and pregnancies

explanation: While abstinence is important, withholding practical information about contraception leaves sexually active teens completely unprotected. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h8)

question: Why do clinical wards need to do regular stock checks of their medicines?

options.A: To increase the speed at which pharmaceutical companies deliver orders
options.B: To prove to hospital management that nurses have extra free time
options.C: To ensure the medicine cupboards look neat and tidy for visitors
options.D: To catch and remove expired drugs before they reach patients

explanation: Regular checks help you spot expired or spoiling medicines early so patients never receive substandard care. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T4#GNS125_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why do doctors order antibody blood tests like rheumatoid factor when checking joint pain?

options.A: To evaluate how well the kidneys filter waste products
options.B: To measure the exact daily amount of calcium in the bones
options.C: To determine if the client has an active bacterial wound infection
options.D: To check for specific proteins that indicate an autoimmune attack

explanation: Tests like rheumatoid factor look for rogue proteins that show the immune system is mistakenly attacking the body's own healthy joint tissues. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h5)

question: What is a major risk of trusting pulse oximetry all by itself during a respiratory check?

options.A: Oxygen readings change too slowly to be useful
options.B: Oxygen levels can look fine while carbon dioxide is dangerously high
options.C: Pulse oximeters cannot measure heart rate accurately
options.D: High oxygen readings mean the patient is completely cured

explanation: A great oxygen saturation score doesn't mean they are blowing off carbon dioxide well. Always look at the whole patient! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the standard clinical definition for diagnosing a patient with epilepsy?

options.A: A single febrile seizure during childhood
options.B: Two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart
options.C: Three provoked seizures within a single week
options.D: One unprovoked seizure with a normal EEG

explanation: Epilepsy is generally diagnosed when a person has had at least two unprovoked seizures that happened more than 24 hours apart. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T9#GNS222_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why is pink and frothy sputum an urgent sign that nurses must report immediately?

options.A: It is a normal byproduct of taking cough syrup
options.B: It means the patient is swallowing too much saliva
options.C: It indicates fluid backing up into the air sacs from the heart
options.D: It shows the patient has been smoking too many cigarettes

explanation: Well done! Pink and frothy sputum tells us fluid is leaking into the tiny air sacs in the lungs (pulmonary edema)—definitely something you want to catch and report fast! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why do community health nurses care about things like housing and clean water?

options.A: These environmental factors directly shape the health outcomes of the population
options.B: Nurses are primarily trained as civil and structural engineers
options.C: It is a legal requirement for opening a new hospital ward
options.D: It lowers the cost of purchasing expensive surgical instruments

explanation: Great job thinking about the big picture! Social factors like clean water and good housing are the bedrock of community wellness. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h1)

question: What instruction should you give your patient right before you pull out an NG tube?

options.A: Breathe in and out through your mouth very fast
options.B: Suck on a hard candy immediately
options.C: Take a deep breath and hold it
options.D: Cough as hard as you can

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for someone living with long-term Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Completely restoring lost declarative memories from childhood
options.B: Training the brain to regrow lost neurons through intense puzzles
options.C: Teaching the patient how to fabricate stories more convincingly
options.D: Maximizing remaining functional independence using environmental aids

explanation: Since memory loss sticks around, we focus on helping them stay safe and independent using daily routines, calendars, and friendly cues. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h8)

question: What happens to oxygen and carbon dioxide levels in the body during asphyxia?

options.A: High nitrogen and low carbon dioxide
options.B: Low nitrogen and high oxygen
options.C: High oxygen and low carbon dioxide
options.D: Low oxygen and high carbon dioxide

question: What is a major infectious cause of scar tissue that leads to ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Urinary tract infection
options.B: Bacterial vaginosis
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Pelvic inflammatory disease causes inflammation and scarring in the fallopian tubes, blocking the normal path of a fertilized egg. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h3)

question: Which substance is most widely available and socially accepted among young people?

options.A: Methamphetamine
options.B: Alcohol
options.C: Heroin
options.D: Cocain

explanation: Correct! Alcohol is the most commonly consumed and socially tolerated substance among adolescents, both globally and right here at home. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h2)

question: Why is the home environment generally considered beneficial for a recovering child?

options.A: It removes the need for parents to monitor vital signs.
options.B: It provides the same advanced surgical tools as an operating room.
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of household infections.
options.D: It lowers psychological stress and supports normal development.

explanation: Spot on! Being around family and familiar toys helps kids feel secure, easing the fear and stress that often come with being sick. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is the main use of a yellow, puncture-proof safety box?

options.A: To collect expired liquid syrups and chemical disinfectants safely
options.B: To store office stationery and confidential patient case notes
options.C: To hold organic kitchen food leftovers from the hospital cafeteria
options.D: To safely contain needles and sharps without risk of piercing

explanation: Great job! Safety boxes have hard walls so needles can't poke through and accidentally injure hospital staff. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h5)

question: After leaving the baby's heart, where does the freshest, most oxygen-rich blood go first?

options.A: Kidneys and adrenal glands
options.B: Lower extremities and feet
options.C: Brain and upper body
options.D: Large and small intestines

explanation: That makes total sense when you think about it: the brain and head need top priority for oxygen to grow rapidly during pregnancy! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h3)

question: Why is inhalation therapy often preferred over oral medications for lung conditions?

options.A: It guarantees 100 percent absorption into the bloodstream
options.B: It works faster locally and reduces widespread side effects
options.C: It is completely free of any potential complications
options.D: It never requires patient coordination or special training

explanation: Targeting the lungs directly means smaller doses can treat the problem without affecting the rest of the body as heavily. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is measuring hourly urine output so important when monitoring a bleeding patient?

options.A: It is a reliable indicator of whether vital organs are receiving enough blood
options.B: It prevents the urinary bladder from becoming overstretched
options.C: It tells the nurse the exact blood type of the patient
options.D: It proves that the patient is drinking enough water by mouth

explanation: The kidneys are sensitive to drops in blood volume; if urine output falls, it means perfusion to major organs is inadequate. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h4)

question: A nurse sets up a quick blood sugar check station at the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primordial prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Awesome! Screening tests help us spot hidden or early-stage health issues, making this secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h4)

question: If a doctor suspects a hole in the patient's gut, what type of contrast dye is used instead of barium?

options.A: Thick barium paste
options.B: Water-soluble contrast
options.C: Oily contrast dye
options.D: Air contrast only

explanation: Brilliant! Water-soluble dyes are much safer because if they leak out, the body can easily absorb them without causing a major crisis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why is the intravenous route preferred over oral medications during a severe medical emergency?

options.A: It is completely painless for the patient
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from filtering drugs
options.C: It provides immediate bioavailability
options.D: It completely avoids the need for a nurse

explanation: Injecting medication directly into the vein skips absorption time, making it act instantly when seconds matter. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is a major long-term danger of untreated, persistent severe tachycardia?

options.A: Permanent freezing of the sinoatrial node pacemaker cells
options.B: Thickening of the heart valves due to high-speed blood flow
options.C: Heart muscle fatigue and possible heart failure due to constant strain
options.D: Complete blockage of all peripheral veins in the extremities

explanation: Just like running a car engine at top speed without a break, forcing the heart to race constantly wears it out over time, leading to muscle fatigue and heart failure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h7)

question: A patient with hypertension stops taking their drugs because their blood pressure went back to normal. What is this called?

options.A: Erratic adherence
options.B: Creative adjustment
options.C: Premature discontinuation
options.D: Primary non-fulfillment

question: How would you best describe a 'geopolitical' community?

options.A: A religious group meeting across multiple countries

options.C: Physical and natural boundaries like rivers or city limits
options.D: A shared hobby or professional career path

question: What is the true relationship between FGM and major world religions?

options.A: Christian scriptures require the procedure for moral purity
options.B: FGM is a cultural practice falsely linked to religious texts
options.C: The Holy Quran explicitly commands all families to perform FGM
options.D: Islamic law strictly forbids any form of traditional surgery

question: Which of these is NOT something a bedside nurse is supposed to do during diagnostic tests?

question: When we classify a joint by its 'function', what are we actually describing?

options.A: How much movement the joint allows

question: Why is the involvement of religious and traditional leaders crucial for eliminating harmful practices?

options.A: They control the primary budgets for hospital construction
options.B: They possess formal medical licenses to treat surgical complications
options.C: They hold significant moral authority and influence community behavior
options.D: They are legally mandated to act as local health inspectors

explanation: Community members listen closely to religious and traditional elders, making their support vital for shifting cultural norms. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h4)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention programs in substance abuse control?

options.A: Stopping individuals from ever experimenting with harmful drugs in the first place
options.B: Helping long-term recovering addicts find stable employment after treatment
options.C: Imposing strict criminal prison sentences on local drug traffickers
options.D: Providing immediate emergency detox in a specialized intensive care unit

explanation: Primary prevention is all about stopping the issue before it starts by educating healthy populations. Prevention is always better than cure! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h3)

question: A clinic patient has severe anxiety because her partner constantly threatens and stalks her. How should a nurse view this situation under the VAPP Act?

question: Which of these is required for a patient's informed consent to be legally valid?

question: Why should nurses recommend locally available, affordable foods during nutritional counseling?

question: Which of these conditions is a true medical emergency involving sudden, dangerous swelling of the upper airway?

question: Why is finding out an HIV status early through HCT so helpful for a patient?

question: How does palliative fatigue differ from normal everyday tiredness?

question: What is the main purpose of a clean delivery kit in community health?

question: What is the best reason to use open-ended questions when talking with a PAC patient?

question: Why is it important to watch the client's face during passive exercises?

question: Why is keeping blood pressure under control so important for preventing strokes?

question: Which core nursing ethic requires you to keep a survivor's identity and story strictly secret?

question: Which clinical finding is an early indicator of hypovolemic shock?

question: What is a primary focus for advancing critical care nursing in resource-limited settings like Nigeria?

question: What makes professional malpractice different from general negligence?

question: What is a major danger of excessive cohesiveness in a healthcare team?

question: A nurse is teaching an asthma patient how to use an inhaler. What is the best way to make sure the teaching worked?

question: Nail clubbing (where fingertips widen and nails curve) is most commonly linked to which health issue?

question: Why do nurses apply universal precautions to every patient, not just those with a known infection?

question: What is the main superpower of herd immunity in a community?

options.B: It guarantees that every single person in the population will never get infected
options.C: It protects vulnerable individuals who cannot be vaccinated by breaking the transmission chain
options.D: It eliminates all environmental sources of bacteria within a specific geographical area

explanation: When almost everyone around is immune, the germ has nowhere to jump. This creates a protective shield around babies or sick folks who can't take vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T79#GNS214_U1_T79_h5)

question: How is segmentation different from peristalsis in the digestive tract?

options.A: Segmentation occurs only in the stomach, while peristalsis happens in the colon.
options.B: Segmentation relies on skeletal muscle, while peristalsis uses smooth muscle.
options.C: Segmentation stops digestion, while peristalsis speeds up absorption.
options.D: Segmentation mixes food back and forth, while peristalsis pushes food forward.

explanation: Think of peristalsis as a wave pushing food down a slide, while segmentation is more like stirring soup back and forth to mix it thoroughly with digestive juices! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h1)

question: What type of medication must be given for a few weeks before surgery to remove a pheochromocytoma?

options.A: Alpha-blockers
options.B: Potassium supplements
options.C: Insulin infusions
options.D: Corticosteroids

explanation: Before surgeons touch a pheochromocytoma, the patient needs alpha-blockers to keep their blood vessels relaxed and prevent dangerous blood pressure spikes during the operation. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T12#GNS222_U2_T12_h7)

question: Why do normal lab test values change when a woman is pregnant?

options.A: Pregnant women have a slower metabolic rate overall
options.B: Blood cells shrink in size during the first trimester
options.C: The laboratory equipment is calibrated differently for women
options.D: Pregnancy hormones significantly alter baseline body chemistry

explanation: Think of pregnancy as a total body makeover! Because hormones shift so much, the normal lab ranges you use for non-pregnant patients simply don't apply here. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h1)

question: What is the major danger if a deep vein thrombosis (DVT) breaks free from a leg vein?

options.A: It can travel to the lungs and cause a pulmonary embolism.
options.B: It reverses blood flow and causes high blood pressure.
options.C: It will dissolve harmlessly inside the liver tissues.
options.D: It causes immediate gangrene in the toes of that foot.

explanation: A loose clot becomes a travelling troublemaker (embolus), riding the bloodstream straight into the lungs where it can block vital blood flow. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h5)

question: What is the biggest danger of leaving dysphagia untreated in a patient?

options.A: Chronic skin rashes
options.B: Permanent hearing loss
options.C: Sudden kidney failure
options.D: Aspiration pneumonia

explanation: When food or drink slips down the wrong pipe into the lungs, it brings bacteria right along with it. This is why watching how patients swallow is so crucial! [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h4)

question: How should a nurse respond when a teen shares a wild cultural myth about birth control?

options.A: Laugh to show how ridiculous the rumor sounds to professionals
options.B: Scold the teenager for believing such foolish stories in public
options.C: Gently validate their concern and provide accurate, simple facts
options.D: Ignore the statement entirely and prescribe whatever is easiest

explanation: Always meet patients with kindness, not judgment. Listening first helps you correct misinformation effectively. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h7)

question: Why do people commonly take protein powder supplements?

options.A: To treat acute bacterial infections in the respiratory tract
options.B: To support muscle growth and repair after physical exercise
options.C: To permanently lower high blood pressure levels
options.D: To cure chronic iron-deficiency anemia quickly

explanation: Protein gives the body the building blocks (amino acids) it needs to repair and build up muscle tissue after a workout. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h3)

question: An adolescent health clinic welcomes all teenagers regardless of their financial status or background. Which core characteristic is this clinic showing?

options.A: Selective
options.B: Commercial
options.C: Exclusive
options.D: Equitable

explanation: Equitable care simply means fair treatment for every young person, treating everyone with equal care and without any form of discrimination. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T18#GNS312_U3_T18_h2)

question: What is a normal, healthy reason for a small amount of fluid to appear in the Pouch of Douglas?

options.A: Uterine fibroid growth
options.B: Recent ovulation
options.C: Cervical dilation
options.D: Endometrial shedding

explanation: Brilliant! When an egg is released during ovulation, a tiny, totally harmless amount of fluid escapes and pools in the pelvis. Totally normal! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h2)

question: Which Nigerian legislation sets the legal age of marriage at eighteen years?

options.A: The National Health Act
options.B: The Penal Code Act
options.C: The Child Rights Act
options.D: The Matrimonial Causes Decree

explanation: The Child Rights Act explicitly defines a child as anyone under 18 and prohibits marriage at that age. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h7)

question: A community health nurse notices many young people in her village developing untreated high blood pressure. What action best reflects modern primary health care nursing practice?

options.A: Waiting inside the urban teaching hospital for patients to travel and find her
options.B: Focusing solely on childhood immunizations and ignoring adult health entirely
options.C: Organizing a local screening camp combined with lifestyle and diet counseling
options.D: Telling the villagers that chronic illnesses cannot be managed at the local level

explanation: Proactive community screening and health education bring prevention and early management directly to the people, fulfilling PHC goals. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why do doctors order a D-dimer blood test when checking for a deep vein thrombosis (DVT)?

options.A: To look for protein fragments that show a recent blood clot is breaking down
options.B: To measure blood pressure inside leg veins
options.C: To see plaque buildup inside the aorta
options.D: To check how fast red blood cells settle in a tube

explanation: D-dimer is a leftover protein piece that floats around when the body is dissolving a blood clot. If the test is negative, it's a great clue that a clot isn't lurking there! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h7)

question: Why must a nurse flush a feeding tube before and after giving medication or formula?

options.A: To cool down the internal stomach lining
options.B: To stimulate natural saliva production
options.C: To prevent the tube from clogging
options.D: To increase the patient's daily water weight

explanation: Feeding tubes are narrow and can easily block up with thick formula or crushed meds. A simple water flush keeps everything flowing smoothly. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h5)

question: Which patients should receive Standard Precautions?

options.A: Every patient in the healthcare setting
options.B: Only patients with weak immune systems
options.C: Only patients admitted to the emergency room
options.D: Only patients with confirmed infections

explanation: Always treat every patient with Standard Precautions! We treat everyone as if they could carry an infection, keeping both them and us safe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of involving local community members when planning health programs?

options.A: Health programs become better tailored to solve actual local community problems
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for professional nurses and doctors
options.C: It guarantees that international donor organizations will fund the hospital
options.D: Government health budgets can be reduced to zero

explanation: You nailed it! When locals help plan care, the programs actually tackle the real problems people face every day. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T15#GNS312_U4_T15_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe nursing action after a patient returns from an MRI where they received mild sedation for anxiety?

options.A: Keeping the hospital bed in a low position with rails up
options.B: Allowing the patient to walk unaccompanied to the bathroom
options.C: Monitoring vital signs until the sedation wears off
options.D: Checking for signs of allergic reactions to any contrast dye

explanation: Sedated patients are at a high risk for falls and dizziness, so they should never walk alone until fully recovered. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h6)

question: An older stroke patient says their biggest goal is to walk to the backyard garden to see flowers. How should you use this?

options.A: Ignore the statement because garden visits are not medical milestones
options.B: Tell the patient to pick a standard treadmill speed instead
options.C: Incorporate the garden walk into realistic, patient-centered goal setting
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately since they have outdoor desires

explanation: You've got this! When rehab goals matter personally to the patient, they feel much more motivated to work hard and get better. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h2)

question: What should you do if you find a banned or unclear abbreviation on a patient's drug chart?

options.A: Cross it out and rewrite it using personal shorthand codes
options.B: Guess the intended dose based on the patient's age and weight
options.C: Administer the medication immediately to avoid treatment delays
options.D: Clarify the order with the prescriber before giving the drug

explanation: Safety first! Never guess when an order is unclear. Always contact the prescribing doctor or clinician to verify what they meant before giving the medication. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h5)

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks comes in with high blood pressure and sudden swelling in her face and hands. What should you suspect?

options.A: Early onset gestational diabetes
options.B: Normal physiological edema of pregnancy
options.C: Gestational hypertension or preeclampsia
options.D: Placental abruption with internal bleeding

explanation: New high blood pressure plus sudden swelling after 20 weeks is a major red flag for preeclampsia. Always keep a close eye on your patient's BP readings! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h3)

question: What is the term for a very rapid labor that finishes in less than three hours?

options.A: Protracted labor
options.B: Precipitate labor
options.C: Obstructed labor
options.D: Augmented labor

explanation: Precipitate labor describes an extremely fast delivery caused by low resistance in the soft tissues of the pelvis and cervix, which is common in multiparous women. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T008#GNS226_U4_T008_h4)

question: What should the nurse do if the weights attached to skeletal traction accidentally rest on the floor?

options.A: Leave them on the floor to give the patient a rest
options.B: Lift and rehang the weights so they hang freely
options.C: Remove the traction ropes permanently from the bed frame
options.D: Add an extra five kilograms of weight to compensate

explanation: Traction weights must never touch the floor because ground support removes the pulling force, leading to loss of bone alignment and sudden muscle spasms. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why do nurses do a cultural assessment for patients?

options.A: To satisfy mandatory hospital paperwork requirements only
options.B: To convince the patient to adopt Western medical practices
options.C: To understand the patient's beliefs and values in order to provide individualized care
options.D: To determine the financial income of the patient's household

explanation: Wonderful! Cultural assessments help us respect our patients' traditions and beliefs, making sure our care fits their unique lifestyle. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T1#GNS123_U2_T1_h5)

question: What do we call a disease that is constantly present at a steady baseline level in a specific area?

options.A: Sporadic
options.B: Epidemic
options.C: Pandemic
options.D: Endemic

explanation: Great job! An endemic disease is regularly found within a specific region, maintaining a predictable and steady presence over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h2)

question: What is the main difference between a bone marrow aspiration and a bone marrow biopsy?

options.A: Biopsy checks cell maturity, while aspiration checks bone strength
options.B: Biopsy uses arm veins, while aspiration uses the sternum
options.C: Aspiration needs general anaesthesia, but biopsy does not
options.D: Aspiration takes liquid, while a biopsy takes a solid piece of tissue

explanation: Think of aspiration as taking a fluid sample of the marrow, while a biopsy takes a tiny solid cylinder of bone and marrow to check its structure. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h4)

question: During a gastric lavage, a patient suddenly turns cyanotic, coughs hard, and has a drop in oxygen saturation. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Ask the patient to take deep breaths through their nose
options.B: Stop the procedure immediately and suction the airway
options.C: Instill more wash fluid to clear out any remaining blockages
options.D: Remove the protective endotracheal tube right away

explanation: These signs point to fluid aspiration into the lungs, requiring an immediate halt to fluid instillation and clearing of the airway to restore breathing. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is the standard time frame following the end of a pregnancy for a death to be classified as a maternal death?

options.A: Within 6 months
options.B: Within 7 days
options.C: Within 42 days
options.D: Within 1 year

explanation: A maternal death includes any death occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days following the termination of the pregnancy, provided it is related to the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h1)

question: Why is it dangerous to swallow strong painkillers to hide tummy ache?

options.A: It causes immediate and permanent blindness in all affected adults
options.B: It permanently lowers a patient's normal body temperature
options.C: It can delay the diagnosis of a serious condition like appendicitis
options.D: It automatically cures any underlying infection within a few hours

explanation: Pain is your body's warning alarm! Masking it with painkillers might trick you into thinking you're fine while a serious emergency like appendicitis gets worse. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is a major long-term risk for a woman who has had repeated bouts of salpingitis?

options.A: Chronic swelling of the lower legs
options.B: Development of uterine fibroids
options.C: Permanent cessation of menstruation
options.D: Infertility and ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Scars from repeated infections can block the tubes, making it harder to get pregnant or increasing the risk of an ectopic pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h8)

question: Why must pregnant women avoid self-medication at all costs?

options.A: Pregnancy completely stops the stomach from absorbing pills
options.B: Drugs can cross the placenta and harm the developing foetus
options.C: Pregnant women are immune to all standard pain relievers
options.D: Unprescribed drugs only affect the mother's hair growth

explanation: You nailed it! Many drugs can slip across the placenta barrier and interfere with the safe growth of the unborn baby. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which healthcare professional specializes in testing hearing and fitting hearing aids?

options.A: Ophthalmologist
options.B: Audiologist
options.C: Dietitian
options.D: Podiatrist

explanation: An audiologist is the expert you call for hearing tests, ear diagnoses, and finding the right hearing devices for patients. Easy to remember! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T9#GNS311_U3_T9_h6)

question: During which week of enteric fever are dangerous complications like intestinal bleeding or tears most likely to happen?

options.A: Eighth week
options.B: Third week
options.C: Fifth week
options.D: First week

explanation: Spot on! By the third week, intestinal tissues have taken a heavy beating, raising the risk of bleeding or holes in the bowel. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h6)

question: How do strong cultural preferences for traditional birth attendants usually affect postnatal referrals?

options.A: They ensure all newborn red flags are diagnosed early
options.B: They often cause dangerous delays in seeking formal medical care
options.C: They train primary health nurses in advanced surgical skills
options.D: They help finance hospital transport for emergency cases

explanation: When families trust traditional options first, it can delay them from coming to the clinic until complications become life-threatening. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h7)

question: Why do inherited degenerative brain diseases often change a person's emotions as well as their body?

options.A: The genetic mutations directly damage brain areas controlling mood and personality
options.B: Brain cell loss only happens in areas that control muscle movement
options.C: Medications used for movement problems always cause severe anger
options.D: Patients simply feel sad because they know they have a chronic illness

explanation: Think of it this way: when the disease targets specific brain pathways, it affects both how the body moves and how emotions are regulated. Makes total sense when you picture it! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h1)

question: Which physical change points strongly to long-term high cortisol levels in Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Truncal obesity with thin extremities and a moon face
options.B: Rapid, unexplained weight loss accompanied by low blood pressure
options.C: Permanent darkening of the mucous membranes and gumlines
options.D: Severe generalized muscle wasting and profound skin darkening

explanation: Cortisol loves to move fat around—collecting it on the belly, back of the neck, and round face while making the arms and legs look thinner. You'll spot this look easily in practice! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T12#GNS222_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why does functional decline in degenerative disorders often fluctuate day-to-day?

options.A: Immune systems fight off the genetic code
options.B: Therapists alter medications every morning
options.C: Genetic mutations change their sequence daily
options.D: Patients experience varying levels of fatigue and stiffness

explanation: Factors like exhaustion, muscle stiffness, and small changes in health can cause daily ups and downs in what a patient is able to do. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h2)

question: What is a huge plus of wearing a halo vest compared to lying flat in bed with tongs?

options.A: It allows the patient to sit up and move around safely
options.B: It completely removes the need for pin site cleaning
options.C: It does not require any pins to penetrate the skull bone
options.D: It applies continuous heavy weight without using pulleys

explanation: Halo vests are amazing because they attach the head ring to a body vest, meaning the patient isn't stuck flat in bed all day! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h3)

question: What do we call the emotional exhaustion and burnout nurses feel after constantly caring for trauma and disaster victims?

options.A: Acute physical shock
options.B: Developmental regression
options.C: Somatic conversion
options.D: Compassion fatigue

explanation: Spot on! Compassion fatigue happens when caring for others day in and day out drains your own emotional tank. Always remember to care for yourself, too! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h6)

question: Why must a nurse carefully watch a patient's urine output after starting an anticholinergic anti-spasmodic?

options.A: The drug is filtered out very rapidly by the kidneys
options.B: It prevents the patient from developing severe diarrhea
options.C: It proves the drug is successfully relaxing the stomach
options.D: The medication can cause urinary retention

explanation: Anticholinergics can make it hard for the bladder to squeeze properly, causing urine to get trapped. Always keep an eye on how well your patient is passing urine! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h6)

question: How do we best describe substance intoxication in clinical practice?

options.A: A mild nutritional deficiency resulting from poor diet
options.B: A permanent physical injury caused by chemical toxicity
options.C: A temporary, reversible impairment of mental and physical function
options.D: A lifelong genetic disorder of the central nervous system

explanation: You nailed it! Intoxication is a short-term, reversible state that happens right after someone takes a psychoactive substance. It passes as the body clears the drug. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h1)

question: Why can't we use very heavy weights with skin traction?

options.A: Heavy weights will damage the skin and slip off
options.B: Skin traction requires a surgical operating room
options.C: Heavy weights make the patient fall asleep faster
options.D: Skin bones cannot support heavy metal devices

explanation: Skin is tough, but it's not made to carry heavy loads! Too much weight will cause blisters, tears, or just slip right out of the straps. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h2)

question: A widow visits the clinic two years after her husband passed away, unable to return to work, sleep, or stop crying daily. What condition is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Complicated grief
options.B: Acute depression
options.C: Normal mourning
options.D: Anticipatory grief

explanation: When intense grief symptoms persist for a very long time and severely disrupt daily life, it is classified as complicated grief. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the most important thing to watch out for after a patient has their chest tube removed?

options.A: Mild redness around the edges of the healed skin suture line
options.B: Total daily urine output measured in a graduated container
options.C: Signs of breathing difficulty or the chest problem returning
options.D: Temporary soreness at the chest site when coughing

explanation: Always stay alert! The main worry after removal is that air or fluid might start building up again in the chest. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h8)

question: When anticholinergic drugs block the parasympathetic nervous system, which body response naturally takes over?

options.A: Normal resting state
options.B: Fight-or-flight response
options.C: Basal metabolic state
options.D: Rest and digest response

explanation: You've got it! Blocking the 'rest and digest' system lets the sympathetic 'fight-or-flight' responses take the lead. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h1)

question: How can severe anxiety or fear slow down a mother's labour?

options.A: It releases hormones that slow down or weaken uterine contractions.

options.C: It completely stops the maternal kidneys from producing urine.
options.D: It causes the baby to immediately turn into a breech position.

explanation: High stress floods the body with adrenaline (the fight-or-flight hormone), which can pump the brakes on smooth uterine contractions. Keeping mums calm is real nursing care! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T003#GNS226_U3_T003_h2)

question: What is considered the gold-standard, first-choice treatment for chronic insomnia?

options.A: High-dose benzodiazepines every night
options.B: Complete sensory deprivation therapy
options.C: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I)
options.D: Over-the-counter antihistamines

explanation: CBT-I is the top recommendation! It helps retrain your brain and sleep habits for long-term success without any risk of drug dependence. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h8)

question: What does the "principle of adequacy" mean when planning your learning tasks?

options.A: Changing the clinical ward placement every single week
options.B: Providing enough time and practice for you to master the skill
options.C: Ensuring the activity matches the current economic status of the school
options.D: Selecting tasks that only require reading textbooks in the library

question: Which of these is NOT one of the three social needs in McClelland's theory?

options.A: Need for achievement
options.B: Need for biological survival
options.C: Need for affiliation
options.D: Need for power

explanation: Spot on! McClelland focuses on learned social needs (achievement, affiliation, and power), not basic biological survival. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h6)

question: What clinical state is expected if someone suffers severe damage to their reticular formation?

options.A: Blindness and deafness
options.B: Inability to feel pain
options.C: Coma or unresponsiveness
options.D: Loss of voluntary speech

explanation: Since the reticular formation is responsible for keeping us awake and conscious, serious damage to this area unfortunately leads to a coma. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h4)

question: What is the very first, inactive protein chain made from mRNA during peptide hormone production called?

options.B: A prohormone
options.C: A preprohormone
options.D: A carrier protein

question: Where does the federal VAPP Act automatically apply right after being signed?

options.A: Lagos State only
options.B: All thirty-six states simultaneously
options.C: Rural communities only
options.D: Federal Capital Territory, Abuja

question: What does 'intrinsic sphincter deficiency' mean?

options.A: Blockage of urine flow by the prostate gland

options.C: A temporary infection lining the urinary tract
options.D: Overactivity of the main bladder muscle

question: Why do we need a team approach when caring for older adults?

options.A: Families refuse to take care of older relatives at home
options.B: Physicians are no longer legally permitted to work alone
options.C: Older adults usually have multiple overlapping health and social issues
options.D: Hospitals require multidisciplinary teams for financial funding

explanation: Aging bodies often deal with several health challenges at once. Working as a team brings different experts together to handle these complex needs much better than any single person could! [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h1)

question: How should a nurse figure out how much pain a patient is feeling?

options.A: By guessing based on the size of the tumor visible on scans
options.B: By checking how much medication the doctor prescribed
options.C: By measuring changes in the patient's blood pressure and pulse
options.D: By believing the patient's own report of their pain

explanation: Always trust your patient! Pain is a personal experience, and how they say they feel is the most reliable guide we have. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which muscle site is generally considered the safest and most recommended for adult IM injections?

options.A: Dorsogluteal
options.B: Deltoid
options.C: Ventrogluteal
options.D: Vastus lateralis

explanation: Great clinical choice! The ventrogluteal site is a superstar because it stays far away from major nerves and big blood vessels, making it the safest spot on an adult for deep shots. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is usually the very first sign a patient notices with oesophageal cancer?

options.A: Sudden vomiting of bright red blood
options.B: Progressive difficulty swallowing solids
options.C: Severe burning pain right after eating
options.D: Uncontrollable hiccups lasting days

question: You previously referred a postpartum mother for family planning. During her baby's immunization visit, what should you do?

options.A: Assume she went and make no further mention of the referral
options.B: Scold her publicly for failing to attend the scheduled appointment
options.C: Resend the exact same referral letter without speaking to her
options.D: Ask the client if she successfully visited the family planning clinic

explanation: Following up during routine visits shows you care and helps ensure she gets the support she needs for her family goals. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h7)

question: What unit of measurement is typically used when programming an electronic infusion pump?

options.C: Milliliters per hour (mL/hr)
options.D: Liters per 24 hours (L/day)

question: What is the main job of epinephrine when used during a cardiac arrest?

options.A: Stimulates heart rate and contraction force
options.B: Lowers blood pressure by relaxing blood vessels
options.C: Relaxes the airway to help the patient breathe
options.D: Thins the blood to prevent dangerous clots

question: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in the human body?
